Dogwood.description:
A Dogwood policy set (Cedar, and ``when temporal`` over the session's events), AC-42.

Read as it is loaded: the temporal clauses parsed, AgentCore's quotas held
(20 temporal policies, 3 temporal operators in one, a 24-hour window at
most) and, when ``cedarpy`` is installed, the Cedar parsed too.

mode.description: enforce: what the set denies is refused; log_only: decided and recorded, then let through.
mode.title: Mode

policies.description: The policy set, as AgentCore Policy takes it: permit and forbid over Datalayer::User principals, Datalayer::Action::"<server>___<tool>" actions and the Datalayer::Runtime resource, with when temporal { formerly within | since within | count | sum } over the session's request, response and error events. Deny by default; a forbid overrides any permit.
policies.title: Policies

Dogwood.title: Dogwood

FirewallCeiling.description:
An organization's ``firewall``: the most any of its agents may be granted.

The same grammar as :class:`FirewallRules`. A direction left out (``None``)
bounds nothing; an empty egress list grants nothing beyond the base layer,
an empty ingress list nothing beyond ``platform``. ``*`` allows ``*``.
:func:`agent_shield.firewall.bounds.bounded` holds an agent's rules to it.

egress.description: The most an agent's egress may be: '*' (any public address) alone, or exact hosts, host:port, IPv4 addresses, CIDRs, each with an optional :port. Left out bounds nothing; empty grants nothing beyond the platform's endpoints.
egress.title: Egress

ingress.description: The most an agent's ingress may be: '*', or addresses and CIDRs with an optional :port. 'platform' is always kept. Left out bounds nothing; empty keeps 'platform' only.
ingress.title: Ingress

FirewallCeiling.title: FirewallCeiling

Grant.description: One line of the ``local`` authorizer: who may do what to what, as patterns (fnmatch).

relation.description: can_read, can_execute, can_call, can_act, or an action class
relation.title: Relation

Grant.title: Grant

Harnesses.description: The harnesses an organization admits, and whose credentials run them.

admit.description: Harness ids of the catalogue this scope admits; empty admits every registered harness.
admit.title: Admit

credentials.description: Whose key runs a harness: the account's own declared secret, the platform's, or either.
credentials.title: Credentials

Harnesses.title: Harnesses

Limits.description:
The stateful limits of a session.

Three count the harness's actions; two count what its model costs: the
**model budget** in tokens and the **spend** in credits (the deployment's
spend limit; 100 credits are one USD). Each has a soft threshold, where the
next call asks the person, and a hard one, where each further call is
refused and the sentence says what would let it go on.

model_tokens.description: The model budget: tokens the session's model requests spend, in and out.

spend.description: The spend limit: credits the session spends on models (100 credits a USD).

Limits.title: Limits

Mcp.description: The MCP servers the agent is lent, by name; everything else is cut from session/new.
Mcp.title: Mcp

Network.description: What the agent may reach over the network, through the Shield.

fetch.description: Hosts a fetch may reach (exact host, or *.example.com); empty refuses every fetch.
fetch.title: Fetch

Network.title: Network

package.description: The Rego package answering decision and context.
package.title: Package

rate.description: How many, at most, in each period.
rate.title: Rate

RateLimits.description:
What each person may spend through the organization's AgentCore Gateways (AC-45).

Per user — the Gateway's OAuth subject, or its IAM principal — across its
tools, models and agents, as AgentCore's Gateway rate limits count them. The
Shield does not count these in process: they are pushed to the Gateways of an
organization that runs on AgentCore.

connections.description: Connections a person holds open to a Gateway.

requests.description: Requests a person makes through a Gateway.

RateLimits.title: RateLimits

Rule.description: One line of a policy: what it matches and what it decides.

classes.description: The classes the rule names; empty names every class.
classes.title: Classes

commands.description: Regular expressions on the whole command line; any matches.
commands.title: Commands

kinds.description: The ACP tool kinds the rule names; empty names every kind.
kinds.title: Kinds

name.description: A short name; every sentence quotes it.
name.title: Name

paths.description: Globs on the path relative to the workspace (fnmatch); any matches.
paths.title: Paths

where.description: inside: only a path inside the workspace; outside: only one outside; any: both, and actions with no path.
where.title: Where

Rule.title: Rule

Threshold.description: A soft threshold asks once; a hard one refuses each call that would cross it.
Threshold.title: Threshold

authorize.description: The classes that need an authorizer's allow beside the Rules: a deny wins over any Rule, an unreachable authorizer is a deny. Empty needs none (local-only); Datalayer's documents name read, write, execute, send and buy.
authorize.title: Authorize

authorizer.description: The decision point a standalone Shield asks: local (grants in this file), openfga {url, store, model}, authzen {url}, opa {url, package} or cedar {policies}. On Datalayer the authorizer is IAM's and a managed document names none.

dogwood.description: A Dogwood policy set deciding every classed action over the session's history (AgentCore Policy's language): a deny wins over any Rule, as the authorizer's does; an allow only lets the Rules decide.

expires.description: When a pulled copy stops being honoured.
expires.title: Expires

firewall.description: The organization's ceiling on its agents' firewall rules (policy.shield): the most any agent may be granted, egress and ingress, '*' allowing '*'. An organization document's alone.

rate_limits.description: Per user, across tools, models and agents: the requests, tokens and connections each person may spend per second or per minute through the organization's AgentCore Gateways, pushed to them as Gateway rate limits. An organization document's alone.
